name: REACH
description: Rare malignant cells in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), including circulating tumor cells (CTCs), minimal residual disease (MRD) cells, and small malignant populations in heterogeneous tumor microenvironments (TME), represent an important clinical challenge. These cells occur at very low frequency, requiring separation from a large non-malignant background. Existing methods show inconsistent evaluation, using different datasets, label definitions, prevalence settings, scoring strategies, and failure handling. We present Rare-cell Evaluation Across Cancer Heterogeneity (REACH), treating inter-lineage rare malignant cell detection as an imbalanced ranking task. REACH benchmarks CNV-supported malignant cells (P_HC) against immune, stromal, and normal epithelial cells (B_HC), modeling the CTC and MRD screening setting. REACH excludes intra-lineage state discovery, including drug-tolerant persisters, epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), and transitional malignant states, evaluating these separately in Track F. REACH combines confidence tiered multi-arm labels with five evaluation tracks, covering controlled real spike-ins, synthetic Splatter stress tests, null background controls, natural blood/CTC prevalence, and supervised label noise diagnostics. Applying standardized method wrappers, fallback-aware metrics, non-parametric statistics, and audited figure regeneration, REACH provides a reproducible evaluation framework.
